lines.speaker: Protesilaus
lines.text: O master and king, our own Zeus, and you, daughter of Demeter — don’t turn away a lover’s request.

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: What do you need from us? Who are you, anyway?

lines.speaker: Protesilaus
lines.text: I’m Protesilaus, son of Iphiclus, from Phylace. I fought with the Achaeans and was the first to die at Troy. All I ask is to be let go for a little while to live again.

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: That’s the one desire every dead man has, Protesilaus. But none of them get it.

lines.speaker: Protesilaus
lines.text: It’s not life I want, Hades. It’s my wife. I left her newly married in our chamber when I sailed away, and then the poor fool died on the beach at Hector’s hands. Her love is eating away at me, master. I just want to see her for a moment and come back down.

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: Didn’t you drink from the Lethe, Protesilaus?

lines.speaker: Protesilaus
lines.text: I did, master. But this is too much.

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: Then wait. She’ll come eventually. No need for you to go up.

lines.speaker: Protesilaus
lines.text: I can’t bear the waiting, Pluto. You’ve been in love yourself. You know what it’s like.

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: And what good will one day do you? You’ll just come back and start mourning all over again.

lines.speaker: Protesilaus
lines.text: I think I can persuade her to come with me. Then you’ll get two corpses instead of one.

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: That’s not allowed. It’s never happened.

lines.speaker: Protesilaus
lines.text: Let me remind you, Pluto. You gave Eurydice back to Orpheus for this very reason. And you sent my kinswoman Alcestis with Heracles as a favor.

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: And you want to show up to your beautiful bride looking like this? A bare, ugly skull? How’s she supposed to recognize you? She’ll be terrified, I know it, and run away. You’ll have made the whole trip for nothing.

lines.speaker: Persephone
lines.text: Then fix that too, husband. Tell Hermes, once Protesilaus is back in the light, to tap him with his staff and turn him into the handsome young man he was on his wedding day.

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: Since Persephone agrees, take him up again and make him a bridegroom. But remember: one day only.
